source.title: Problem-Dependent Power of Quantum Neural Networks on Multiclass Classification.
source.authors: Yuxuan Du; Yi-Bo Yang; Da-Cheng Tao; Min-Hsiu Hsieh

record.file_problem: The paper and supplementary material are present. Some equations and figures are flattened or garbled in the web text, but the relevant results are also described in text.
record.tranche_reason: The study reports its own results that quantum classifiers have a U-shaped risk curve rather than double descent, and it compares capacity sweeps for quantum and classical classifiers.
record.gate_note: The paper also describes a proposed algorithm that varies sample count, parameter count, and epochs, but those algorithm settings are not results of a sample-size sweep. Cited double-descent findings are not recorded as study results.
record.test_reason: The study argues in theory (Corollary 1) and reports fitted risk-vs-parameter sweeps showing that quantum classifiers (QCs) follow a U-shaped risk curve rather than double descent. This directly qualifies V4's claim that risk falls again past interpolation across model classes. Small MLP and CNN comparators give weaker evidence bearing on V1.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that QC risk is dominated by training loss rather than generalization error. Because deep (2-design) circuits concentrate outputs and raise empirical risk, they argue QCs follow a U-shaped risk curve unlike the double descent of classical networks, so over-parameterization can hurt QCs. They add that QCs beat an MLP on parity but lose to a CNN on Fashion-MNIST. They attribute the missing MLP double descent to limited training data.
record.recipe_differences: The study analyzes quantum classifiers and compares fitted risk curves with classical neural models; its numerical curves use polynomial fitting and are not a reproduction of the original deep-network experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported outcomes vary with dataset and classifier: QCs have different performance on parity and Fashion-MNIST, and the MLP's double-descent curve is absent in the limited-data parity setting.

fits_no_version.finding: Feature-state geometry metrics M1 (within-class spread) and M2 (between-class overlap) fall during training for mid-depth QCs on parity, but not for shallow/deep ones or on Fashion-MNIST (Figs. J.8, J.10).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Quantum classifiers with near-zero training loss show neural-collapse-like feature geometry, and only at intermediate depth.

record.problems: The numerical datasets are small (64 parity examples and 180 Fashion-MNIST examples); the Fashion-MNIST experiments use 3 repetitions. Risk curves are fitted and shown in figures without numerical curve values in the text. The CNN size result is reported as accuracy rather than directly as test error.
record.rows_left_out: No separate row for the Fashion-MNIST QC point at Nt = 1500: the text reports about 50% train and test accuracy and comparison with CNN, but it does not establish a separate curve-shape result. No numerical values were extracted from the risk-curve figures.

untested.parts: Peak location near the interpolation threshold; deep networks at realistic scale; label-noise settings. Only a tiny MLP on parity and a small CNN sweep are reported.
Not tested; no epoch-wise risk curve is examined for a peak.
Only QCs (hardware-efficient ansatz) plus small classical comparators on two tiny datasets; no random-feature, kernel or tree models.
Not tested; no label-noise or regularization sweep.

missing.what: QC train/test accuracy vs layer number on parity: L=2-4 reach 100% within 25 epochs, L=1 stays near 50%, L=7 overfits. This is the unfitted evidence behind the U shape.
QC accuracy vs layer number on Fashion-MNIST: best about 30% at L=25-100 (750-3000 params), about 15% otherwise. The training set is never fit, which conflicts with the main text's '50% at Nt=1500'.
missing.locator: SM J.2, Fig. J.11(a); main text Numerical results

missing.what: Theoretical argument (Corollary 1): 2-design ansatz/encoding concentrates outputs, so over-parameterization raises empirical risk, implying a U-shaped curve for QCs.
missing.locator: Main text 'U-shaped risk curve' section; SM G

record.verdict_notes: Neither original source is this study. r5's 'reversed' state was wrong: rising CNN accuracy is compatible with double descent, and the sweep cannot locate a threshold. The V4 label on r5 was dropped because r5 is linked only to V1 and is undetermined. The datasets are tiny (48 and 90 training examples), the risk curves are polynomial fits shown only in figures, and main-text and SM accuracies for the Fashion-MNIST QC disagree (about 50% vs about 30%).

versions.untested_parts: The Fashion-MNIST CNN capacity sweep reports test accuracy, not a direct risk curve, and does not locate an interpolation threshold or peak.
The reported epoch trajectory is for the parity-dataset QC; other models and datasets are not assessed for epoch-wise double descent.
No reported result tests whether increasing training sample count near an interpolation threshold raises test error.
The reported capacity results cover selected QCs, an MLP, and a CNN on two small datasets, not model classes generally.
No single effective-complexity measure is tested as predicting peak location across model size, epochs, and sample count.
The study does not test peak dependence on label noise, multiple or triple descent, or disappearance under optimally tuned regularization.
The study does not re-express a second descent using an effective parameter count.

rows.subject: QC
rows.operation_detail: Tracked the parity-classification learning trajectory over epochs.
rows.measure: Average train and test accuracy, and loss, over training epochs
rows.value: Average train (test) accuracy rose from 44.1% to 100% within 22 epochs; loss decreased from 0.26 to 4×10−5.
rows.uncertainty: Variance is shown as a shaded region in Fig. 2(a); magnitude not stated.
rows.note: The reported accuracy trajectory improves over training rather than showing the claimed fall-rise-fall test-error pattern.
rows.check: This is a 22-epoch learning curve of one QC (Nt=54) on a noiseless parity task where test accuracy reaches 100%. It shows the model can learn the task; it is not an epoch-wise double-descent test. A QC is also not the deep-network setting V2 describes. The text does not separate train and test values ('train (test) accuracy').

rows.subject: QC
rows.size_stated: Nt varied over [20, 140]; valley reported around Nt = 70
rows.operation_detail: Fitted the QC risk curve while varying the number of trainable parameters.
rows.measure: Fitted risk versus number of trainable parameters
rows.note: The text says the QC outperforms the MLP for Nt ∈ [20, 140] and its risk valley is around Nt = 70. The paper characterizes QC risk curves as U-shaped, not double-descent.
rows.check: State should be absent, not reversed: the second descent past interpolation does not appear (fitted U shape, valley near Nt=70, train n=48). Values are figure-only and the curve is a polynomial fit to few points, so the shape partly depends on the fitting choice. Fig. J.9(a) supports it: L=2-4 reach 100% accuracy, while L=7 (about 126 params) overfits.

source_check.locator_found: Main text, Numerical results; Fig. 2(b); SM J, Curve fitting method.

rows.subject: MLP
rows.size_stated: Hidden-neuron count h ranged from 1 to 18
rows.operation_detail: Compared a fitted risk curve across MLP sizes on the parity dataset.
rows.measure: Fitted risk versus model size; test accuracy also reported
rows.value: The text says the double-descent curve disappeared; test accuracy was no higher than 55%. Risk-curve values: figure only.
rows.locator: Main text, Numerical results and footnote 101; Fig. 2(b)
rows.note: The authors attribute the missing double-descent curve to limited training data in the parity dataset.
rows.check: Authors state the MLP double-descent curve 'disappeared' and blame limited training data (48 examples). The MLP never learns parity (test accuracy at most 55%), and its train accuracy is not given, so it is unclear whether interpolation was reached. The risk-curve values are figure-only.

source_check.locator_found: Footnote 101; Fig. 2(b); SM J.1, learning dynamics of QC and MLP, accompanying Fig. J.9(b).

rows.subject: QC
rows.operation_detail: Fitted the QC risk curve while varying the number of trainable parameters.
rows.measure: Fitted risk versus number of trainable parameters
rows.uncertainty: Three repetitions per setting; numerical uncertainty not stated.
rows.note: The paper describes QC risk as U-shaped; it also reports that at Nt = 1500, train and test accuracy are about 50%.
rows.check: The QC never fits the training set on Fashion-MNIST: SM says best train/test accuracy is about 30%, and about 15% outside L=25-100. The main text instead says about 50% at Nt=1500, which is inconsistent. With no interpolation, the rising risk reflects trainability (barren plateaus), not behaviour past an interpolation threshold. Values are figure-only.

rows.subject: CNN
rows.size_stated: Second-layer output channels: 2, 6, 15, 30, 50, 75; corresponding parameter counts stated as 860, 1284, 2238, 3828, 5948, and 8598
rows.operation_detail: Varied the number of CNN output channels and reported train and test accuracy.
rows.measure: Train and test accuracy versus model size
rows.value: Train and test accuracies are described as steadily growing with increased channel count; when the second-layer channel count is not less than 6, both exceed 60%.
rows.uncertainty: Three repetitions per setting; numerical uncertainty not stated.
rows.locator: Supplementary Material SM J, Simulation results for Fashion-MNIST; Fig. J.11(b)
rows.note: Increasing test accuracy corresponds to decreasing test error; the reported capacity trend does not show the claimed peak and subsequent decline in accuracy.
rows.check: Reversed is wrong. Steadily rising accuracy (lower error) is what the post-threshold descent predicts. The sweep (860-8598 params, 90 train examples) does not locate an interpolation threshold, and train accuracy is only stated as >60%, so a peak could not be seen. It is a comparator with 3 repetitions and no uncertainty values.

relationships.condition: Quantum classifiers (hardware-efficient ansatz), parity dataset, Nt 20-140
relationships.reason: Past interpolation (n=48), the fitted QC risk rises again in a U shape with no second descent (r2). The authors attribute this to concentration/barren plateaus (Corollary 1), so the version does not cover this model class; this rests on a polynomial fit.
relationships.display_finding: The fitted risk rose in a U-shape beyond interpolation at n=48, which the authors attributed to concentration and barren plateaus.

statements.correction: QC: hardware-efficient ansatz; polynomial least-squares risk fitting; U-shaped risk; valley around Nt=70; QC outperforms MLP over Nt∈[20,140]. Parity training set: 64×0.75=48 examples. QC at Nt=54: 100% train/test accuracy; loss approximately 4×10^-5. MLP h=1–18: test accuracy ≤55%; double descent reported absent; authors attribute absence to limited training data.
statements.problem: The fitted U shape and unsuccessful MLP are reported, but an interpolation threshold for the QC sweep is not established. Parameter count exceeding sample count is the paper's generalization definition of over-parameterization.
